newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms but volumes thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms but volumes thin.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices ended slightly higher onMonday in thin volumes in line with a see-sawing futures market and underpinned by the impending November 1996 contract expiry on Tuesday, traders said.
November IPE futures ended up $0.75 at $220.50, down around $5 from session highs spurred by cold weather in Europe.
Sentiment was hesitant before the expiry amid reports the dominant long in the contract planned to take a lot of material out of northwest Europe and move it to Turkey and Singapore.
Heating oil premiums were stable to slightly firmer and those for low sulphur diesel were steady. Refinery grade heating oil cargoes were discussed at Dec IPE +$8.50/11 for late November.
Traders said end-user demand for heating oil in Germany was muted in hope of price falls. "It's a futures game today. In the physical market there are nearly no buyers," one trade said.
One trader said Far East players were putting together large Russian cargoes for Asian markets, squeezing overall European supply amid colder weather and thereby supporting prices.

"I don't think the supply is around to cover increases in demand," he said. A number of heating oil barges were traded at Nov IPE -$0.75 for late November delivery fob ARA and at an outright price of $225.50, around unchanged from Friday.
